I went there to get one, and as I was deciding what to get, I realized I had forgotten my money at my room.

Conversation went something like, fuck, I forgot my money. Friends says, no problem man, lets just walk back to get it.

I was like, nah, whatever, all I wanted was a coke.

Machine goes into motion, coke drops down.

I was like, oh shit! Free drinks! My friend laughed and said that he was a bit spooked by it. He told me to ask for another one.

I ease myself out of the gym with him, the whole time keeping an eye on the machine.

I think I met a ghost on the Golden Gate Bridge. I walked it everyday to work. It's a mile long. Once you get 1/4 of a mile in all the tourists fade and it gets pretty quiet and empty. On a cold blistering morning I was walking along. Karl (the fog) was so thick you couldn't see more than two feet in front of you. Everyone was bundled up to protect from the high wind. I got just past the first tower. I hadn't past another soul since the tourist shop on the SF side. All of a sudden a man in a short sleeve car mechanic's shirt appears out of no where. He smiles at me and says, "Hello, how are you?". I smile back and say good morning as he passes. Then it dawns on me he was wearing short sleeves and a mechanics uniform (everyone on that walking/bike trail wore comfortable sportsware with a bag or two strapped around them, he had none of this). I immediately turn around to comment on his wardrobe and he was gone. If you have never been to the bridge before you have to realize there is nowhere to go. The walking path is fenced in. If someone walks pass you, you can turn around and they should still be there!

Here is a pic of the spot I was at: http://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/af/Walking_on_the_Golden_Gate_bridge_in_San_Francisco_72.jpg

What are your thoughts on tier lists?

I think they have some merit. While they aren't word of law, the general idea is the same.

Some characters are inherently better than others. No game is perfect when it comes to balance.

I think some people take them way too seriously as if it were law, while aMSa didn't let the melee tier list stop him and he does very well.

What is a tier list?

Not a profound thought, but it's mine.

From SSBWiki:

In gaming, a tier list is a list that ranks all characters based on the strength of their fighting abilities and their potential to win matches under tournament conditions, assuming equal skill on the part of each player. A tier list is decided based on the analysis of the following:

  • The metagame and the effectiveness of the characters' strategies

  • Each character's moveset and statistics

  • Each character's matchup spread

  • Each character's tournament results
Well, then. I like them. I use DOTA 2 tier lists to tell me what players to play if I want a better chance of winning.
Tiers don't bother me if you can gather buffs. You can develop an intuition for overcoming gameplay imbalance with good buffs.

For most games what matters more is how comfortable you are with a character's play style, and what your other team members are playing.

Although I must say in Hearthstone when I used to play, the vast majority of my arena runs would get 2 or 3 wins, with a max of like 5... but when I used tier lists to pick cards, my win rate suddenly jumped up to a minimum of 8 wins. It was a shocking increase, and I watched plenty of streamers and thought I knew how good cards were.
I think they suck , specially in RPGs there is nothing more immersion breaking than gear with a level attached to it.

I think that tier lists are a useful tool, but they can also hurt enjoyment of a game for some people in one way or another. I think, specifically in SSB, that a tier list might stop someone from playing their favorite character just because they're low on the list(though that shouldn't affect people, we know it does, because outside pressure carries a lot of influence.)

I suppose I think it's nice that they exist and that they're a very useful tool, but they have the consequence of deterring people from playing characters they otherwise may have.

How effective is the 'search' feature on Voat?
Oh well. Hopefully they have plans to improve it, in the near future.
If you search for a spoon it works fine. Otherwise it simply looks up submissions with the search term in title or the content of text posts.

Default link style:

.link a.title.may-blank {
 color: #4a4a4a;
 font-weight: bold;
}

Visited links:

.link a.title.may-blank:visited {
 color: #9178d0;
}

Hover state:

.link a.title.may-blank:hover {
 color: #4aabe7;
 text-decoration: none;
}

The default theme is very messy but just overriding these 3 rules should do.

Btw for your header image (#header-img), you should replace http:// with https:// in the imgur URL to avoid a mixed content error. Some browsers may not load your image.
